Definition: of uncertain affinity; much (adverbially):--exceeding, great(-ly), sore, very (+ chiefest).
BiblicalUsage: lían means greatly, very much — rare in the text, and exact where it appears. In Mark 16:2, "And very early in the morning the first [day] of the week"; and in Matthew 27:14, "insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.". In 2 John 1:4, "I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in truth".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe greatly is the word for joy that cannot be measured — John rejoiced greatly to find children walking in truth, and that is still the best news a teacher can hear.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
